headline: CATL'S BIGGEST LITHIUM MINE LOSES ENVIRONMENTAL APPROVAL — Benchmark Cuts 2026 Forecast 49% To 32,000t LCE; Restart Timeline Unclear Into 2027
snippet: CATL's Jianxiawo mine — China's largest lithium mine by capacity — was returned to care-and-maintenance after regulators revoked its Environmental Impact Assessment, triggered by an informal July restart that bypassed an unresolved tailings pond dispute and generated over 70 regulatory complaints. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence cut its 2026 mined output forecast for Jianxiawo from 62,500 to 32,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent — a 49% reduction — with the environmental review potentially extending to Q4 2026 or into 2027, threatening to tip the lithium market from managed surplus into deficit.

headline: BRIXTON METALS DRILLS 12,386 g/t SILVER OVER 0.5m AT LANGIS — Classic Cobalt Camp High-Grade Returns; 155 Holes, 33,858m Completed In 2026
snippet: Brixton Metals Corporation (TSXV: BBB) reported September 2 that hole LM-26-432 at the Langis Silver Project in Cobalt, Ontario intersected 6,199 g/t silver over 1.00 metre from 116.05 m depth, including 0.50 m grading 12,386 g/t silver — among the highest-grade intercepts reported from modern drilling in the Cobalt Silver Camp. The 2026 program has completed 33,858 metres across 155 drill holes targeting the Shaft 6 and other near-surface native silver structures consistent with the historical production that made Cobalt one of the world's top silver districts in the early 20th century.

headline: KENORLAND MINERALS MAIDEN WABIGOON DRILL HITS 204 g/t GOLD — 8 Of 9 Holes Hit Mineralisation; Centerra Gold Option; W2 Shear Confirmed Over Drill-Strike
snippet: Kenorland Minerals Ltd. (TSXV: KLD) announced September 3 assay results from its maiden 4,089-metre, nine-hole diamond drill program at the Western Wabigoon Project in northwestern Ontario — held under option with Centerra Gold — confirming a shear-hosted gold-bearing hydrothermal system in eight of nine holes along the W2 target, with one assay returning 204.34 g/t gold. The systematic intersection of gold-bearing alteration across tested strike length — including a broad 37.75-metre zone at 0.30 g/t Au — confirms the W2 target warrants step-out drilling to locate higher-grade shoots within the corridor.

headline: GREENLAND MINES CLOSES SARFARTOQ RARE EARTHS — Neo Performance Gets 60% Offtake; Project Would Supply 34% Of Non-China NdPr Oxide Annually; Team On Site September
snippet: Greenland Mines Ltd. (NASDAQ: GRML) confirmed the September 1 close of its $35 million acquisition of the Sarfartoq neodymium-praseodymium rare earths project in southwest Greenland, with Neo Performance Materials (TSX: NEO) becoming a strategic shareholder holding offtake rights for up to 60% of future ore or concentrate production for processing at its Estonian separation facility. At planned annual output, the Sarfartoq project's 6.9 Mt Indicated Resource at 1.60% TREO would represent approximately 34% of all NdPr oxide refined outside China in each of nine scheduled operating years; the technical team returns to site in September for infill drilling and pilot metallurgical test work.

headline: 68 DAYS UNTIL CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT PAUSE EXPIRES — Wave 2 Controls Return November 10 Without Renewal; 91% Chinese Grip On Refining Unchanged After Pause Year
snippet: China's one-year suspension of its expanded rare earth export controls — which paused Wave 2 licensing requirements on October 9, 2025 — is set to expire November 10, 2026, giving manufacturers less than 70 days to finalize supply chain contingencies with little certainty China will extend. If the suspension lapses, five additional rare earth elements would simultaneously return to full export control coverage alongside the seven medium and heavy elements already under April 2025 licensing; NdPr oxide surged sixfold in the first half of 2026, and China still controls 91% of global rare earth separation and refining capacity — evidence the one-year pause produced limited structural diversification.

headline: BANK OF AMERICA HOLDS $130/LB URANIUM TARGET — Cameco 'The Warning'; Kazatomprom Cuts Structural Ceiling To 77 Mlbs; Spot At $89.50 As September Surge Ignites
snippet: Bank of America maintained its $130/lb uranium price target for 2027 — 52% above the current $89.50/lb spot — citing Cameco's signal that physical uranium tightness is structural rather than cyclical, driven by skilled-labour scarcity at McArthur River rather than capital constraints. Kazatomprom has reset its 2026 production baseline from 85 million to approximately 77 million pounds, with the option to downflex a further 20% below that level — a permanent supply ceiling reset that, combined with the World Nuclear Association's forecast of reactor requirements more than doubling by 2040, removes the macro preconditions for uranium's bear case.

headline: CANADIAN GOLDFIELDS WRAPS INAUGURAL SWAYZE CENTRAL DRILL — Swayze Greenstone Belt Ontario; Camp Neighbours Sage Gold's Clavos; Assays Pending
snippet: Canadian Goldfields Corp. announced September 2 the completion of its inaugural diamond drilling program at the Swayze Central Gold Project in the Swayze Greenstone Belt of northern Ontario, a belt hosting several past producers and active explorers including Sage Gold's Clavos deposit. The company is awaiting assay results from the laboratory; the completion of first-pass drilling at a previously untested target converts the project from a surface geochemistry anomaly to a drill-tested system, with results to determine whether follow-up programs are warranted this season.

headline: GOLD MINERS STILL 25% UNDERVALUED AFTER RECORD AUGUST — GoldSeek: GDX At 11x Forward Earnings vs. 14x Avg; Mid-Tiers And Juniors The Better Bet Now
snippet: Despite miners' best August since 1994 — the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index up 33% on the month — GoldSeek analysis argues that GDX still trades at approximately 11x forward earnings against a five-year average of 14x, implying a 25% re-rating gap before accounting for the record free cash flow miners will report at $4,470 gold. The piece argues that August's surge was a valuation catch-up, not a blow-off top, and that mid-tier and junior gold miners — historically the sector's best-performing cohort in sustained bull phases — have barely participated yet relative to the large-caps.

headline: RETAIL FLOODS GOLD MINERS: $1.4 BILLION INTO GDX/GLD IN AUGUST BEFORE LAST WEEK — 6th Daily Inflow In 7 Sessions; Institutionals Already In; Full Re-Rate Still Ahead
snippet: Retail investors recorded more than $1.4 billion in combined inflows into GLD, GDX, and GDXJ during August 2026 before the week ending September 4 added further flows, with GDX logging its sixth daily retail inflow in seven trading sessions including a single-day record of $25 million — the largest since February. The analysis argues that institutional accumulation since early 2026 has already driven the sector's first re-rating leg, and that retail participation of this scale typically signals the beginning of the second leg in a sector cycle; the full value-chain re-rating from royalty companies through seniors to mid-tiers and juniors is expected to compound as the trade becomes consensus.

headline: CALIFORNIA LITHIUM VALLEY DREAM FADING — Salton Sea Projects Hit Permitting Wall, Capital Drought Despite Federal Subsidies; Tribal Opposition Unresolved
snippet: CalMatters' September 2026 investigation into the Salton Sea 'lithium valley' — California's bid to establish geothermal brine extraction as a domestic battery metals supply anchor — finds multiple projects stalled by permitting delays, unresolved tribal consultation requirements, infrastructure gaps, and a capital environment where project economics cannot close without subsidies that themselves carry timeline uncertainty. The gap between political ambition and development reality has broader implications for US critical minerals independence strategy as the CATL Jianxiawo EIA revocation and China's export control architecture simultaneously demonstrate the consequences of supply chain concentration in adversarial hands.
